questions.q: Which standard Salesforce object does this lesson say connects Solstice's sales side to its service side?
options: Contact
Campaign
Product2
Asset
questions.explain: Asset tracks the specific product a customer owns; a closed-won Opportunity's line items become Assets, and Case has a standard lookup straight to Asset, linking sales and service.

questions.q: What does `Installation_Job__c` represent in this data model?
options: A manufacturer warranty claim
One scheduled installation or repair visit tied to a Case, an Asset, and a Technician
An extended service plan a customer purchased
A line item on an Opportunity
questions.explain: Installation_Job__c is the custom object for one scheduled visit, with lookups to Case, Asset, and the assigned Technician (User).

questions.q: What does `Service_Contract__c`'s `Coverage_Limit__c` field get checked against, per this lesson?
options: The Warranty_Claim__c record's Claim_Amount__c, by the trigger built in Lesson 9
The Opportunity's total amount
The Case's priority field
The Account's annual revenue
questions.explain: Coverage_Limit__c is the maximum claimable amount under a service contract, and the Lesson 9 trigger checks a Warranty_Claim__c's Claim_Amount__c against it.

questions.q: Why does this lesson use lookup relationships, not master-detail, for all three new custom objects?
options: Lookup relationships are always faster to query than master-detail
Master-detail relationships cannot be created on custom objects
Each child record needs to survive and be reassignable independently of its parent, and none of the relationships should cascade-delete real service history
Salesforce no longer supports master-detail relationships
questions.explain: Master-detail ties a child's existence and security directly to its parent, including cascade delete -- not appropriate here since Installation Jobs, Warranty Claims, and Service Contracts all need to persist and be reassignable independently.

questions.q: Where does `Manufacturer_Claim_Id__c` on `Warranty_Claim__c` get its value from, per this lesson?
options: It is entered manually by the sales rep when the Opportunity is created
It is populated by the ID the manufacturer's API returns once the claim is submitted, covered in Lesson 14
It is copied automatically from the Account's Account Number field
It is a formula field calculated from the Case's creation date
questions.explain: The field holds the ID returned by the manufacturer's API once the claim is submitted -- the REST integration built in Lesson 14.
